reviews.text: Thank you for being kind and taking good care of the dog.

I visited this clinic for the first time in a while because the timing didn't work out with my usual vet. Based on this experience, I will not be using this clinic again.

My dog ​​cried twice during the nail trimming, and when I inquired, the staff member who performed the trimming explained that "he's sensitive, that's why he cried."

Although I was told that the bleeding had stopped despite the nail being cut too short, it started bleeding again after we got home, and my dog ​​kept licking it, so I applied pressure to stop the bleeding here.

I have never heard my dog ​​cry like this at other clinics when having his nails trimmed before.

While I understand that cutting the nails too short can happen, I was most disappointed that the explanation given was simply "because he's sensitive," as if it were just my dog's personality, when in fact the nail was cut too short and bleeding occurred. I think there's a possibility he was crying because he was in pain.

Also, I was concerned that the bleeding started again after we got home, despite being told that it had stopped. Even the next day, he was still bothered by the paw with the short nail and kept trying to lick it.

Furthermore, his eyes were red after the procedure, and the redness was noticeable when I checked them. I'm not sure about the connection to restraint, but since it was a condition I'd never seen before, that also worried me.

Also, during the examination, I was told that they would prescribe an ointment for pyoderma, but at the time of payment, I was told, "You might not need the medication, but we'll give it to you if you need it." When I requested the medication, it was covered by insurance, and as a result, the bill was cheaper than the initial estimate. I was also concerned that what I was told during the examination differed from what was said at the time of payment.

When I called the next day to inform them of the issue, the person who trimmed my pet's nails apologized repeatedly.

I hope that something similar doesn't happen to other pet owners or their beloved animals in the future.

We highly recommend Dr. Miyagawa!

We're always grateful for his help. He explains things clearly and answers even the smallest questions sincerely.

He's honest about what's unnecessary, and if you're worried, he'll discuss the pros and cons and offer advice.

His working days are limited, so occasionally it's impossible to get an appointment. We understand that, so it's a good idea to know about backup hospitals.
Good service but Japanese language only

2026. [Date Unknown]
I used their services for my annual vaccination. I've trusted Vice Director Ishikawa since I first got my two dogs, so at the time, appointment slots were limited. I asked if it would be alright to have a new doctor examine one of my dogs for the vaccination and a lump on its back. The vaccination went smoothly, but regarding the lump, they said they would perform a biopsy and give me the results in a week. A week later, I received a voicemail, and when I listened to it, it was just a single sentence: "It was a benign lump." I was left speechless, thinking, "What?!"

Confused, I called the vet who examined my dog ​​to ask what kind of lump it was. Initially, he said it was a rash, but I pointed out that a rash and a lump are different. Then he said something like, "It might be a benign lump..." He was an incompetent vet who couldn't even give a conclusion about the examination.

I feel like they shouldn't have had a new male vet, who isn't even listed in their online booking system, make such a diagnosis. It's grounds for a complaint. My trust in the clinic has plummeted.

I wish the deputy director or director had taken responsibility and made a decision, but no decision was made, no advice on future treatment was given, and I was just ripped off.

☆4→☆1

2024
The clinic is clean, and the receptionists and nurses are very polite and polite, leaving a very good impression. Regarding examinations, I feel confident entrusting my pet to Director Takahashi and Deputy Director Ishikawa, but the female doctor who saw my pet in an emergency due to bloody stool was friendly, but she couldn't give a clear answer, and I wouldn't want to go back to her in the future. Regarding fees, I think they are more reasonable than other clinics.

Since it's by appointment only, I think it's safest for very anxious people or those with severely ill dogs and cats to book online and request the director. Secondly, the deputy director. That's my rule now.

Dr. Ishikawa is often in charge of my dog's care, and he is a very reliable doctor. Whenever I bring my dog ​​to this hospital, his symptoms always improve. The different treatment approaches that Dr. Ishikawa has suggested seem to suit my dog ​​very well, and he always saves him from illnesses that are so severe that it's painful for me to watch him suffer. Also, despite being a popular and always busy hospital, they always make time to listen to my concerns and questions. The nurses and reception staff are also very kind, and I felt at ease leaving my dog ​​there this time. Thank you so much. There are several doctors here, so if you make a same-day appointment, you may have the opportunity to meet a doctor you haven't met before. They also do a great job of keeping track of the medical records, so there is no need to go to other hospitals to find a second opinion, and I can continue to bring my dog ​​here with peace of mind.

Shinjuku Animal Hospital is a very reassuring animal hospital where you can feel at ease, thanks to the kind and attentive doctors and staff. They listen carefully to your concerns and questions, and explain tests and treatments clearly, which instills confidence. The hospital is clean and has a calm atmosphere, so your pet can relax relatively well. The reservation and check-in process is smooth, making it easy to visit even with a busy schedule. I would recommend this animal hospital to anyone looking for a hospital where they can confidently entrust their beloved family member.

The prices are also reasonable.

They are flexible and offer various services, including blood tests.

This hospital was designated for the Shinjuku Ward Public Health Center's subsidy program, so I inquired and was told that a health checkup was required before the procedure. I made an appointment and went there. Despite arriving on time for my appointment, I was kept waiting for over 30 minutes. During that time, other animals were waiting and barking, looking frightened and pitiful.

During the examination, even though I had explained both on the questionnaire and verbally that I had come for a health checkup because I had applied for the public health center's subsidy, they asked why I was there today. The assistant or person accompanying them barely helped when they asked me to bring my pet out for weighing.

The doctor was also completely unresponsive.

They repeated the same thing over and over, and everyone just watched because they weren't being given instructions.

I thought, "Ah, this is why we're kept waiting..."

They asked, "We can't perform the surgery without the triple vaccine and flea/tick treatment. What do you want to do?"

I came to request surgery, so if there's no other option, please proceed.

It cost nearly 10,000 yen in addition to the surgery fee. The surgery itself was about 60,000 yen, with the subsidy being only 4,000 yen... I regret not going somewhere else. After this experience is over, I will never go there again.

I'm puzzled as to why it's designated as a hospital.

It was a great animal hospital.
My cat, dog, and bird were well looked after.

My dog, Popo, is always well cared for here.

She had her spaying surgery here last fall, and I was relieved that her recovery went well and the procedure was completed successfully.

They aren't overly friendly, but they are efficient and provide accurate service.

I think it's a trustworthy hospital that fulfills its role as an animal hospital properly.

P.S. There is also parking space for two cars.
